name: MIOSA

modes.label: Sandbox (fixed sizes micro-xl, managed)
modes.note: Hour = published size price (miosa.ai/pricing, 2026-11-08: micro $0.0316, tiny $0.0359, xs $0.0446, small $0.0893, quad $0.1437, medium $0.1785, large $0.357, xl $0.7141) + the size disk at $0.09/GB-month while running ("Storage attached to a machine, while it exists"). Disk per size from /docs/develop/sandboxes/sizing: xs 10, small 10, medium 20, large 40, xl 80 GB; micro, tiny and quad publish no disk, so their hour has no disk part. "Billed to the second while a machine runs, and nothing for compute while it is stopped" (miosa.ai/pricing). timeout_sec default 3600, max 86400; always_on: true disables timeout and idle-timeout enforcement, subject to tenant policy (paid plans). idle_timeout_sec defaults to 1800 s for accounts created on or after 2026-10-11. A paused sandbox "bills no vCPU or RAM, only its disk at the snapshot rate" ($0.018/GB-month).

modes.label: Computer (durable desktop, fixed sizes)
modes.note: Computers cost the same per hour as the sandbox of the same size (miosa.ai/pricing, 2026-11-08) but carry bigger disks (xs 10, small 20, medium 50, large 100, xl 200 GB; /docs/computers/lifecycle), folded in at $0.09/GB-month while running. "A stopped computer is not billed for compute; its disk is billed at $0.018 per GiB-month while it is stopped." (/docs/computers/lifecycle). Restarting resumes from the snapshot.

evidence.quote: Egress: $0.054 per GB, from the first GB

plans.name: Free
plans.note: $0, "$1 of usage every month"; "No overage: machines pause at a $0 balance. Add credits any time from $5." 5 sandboxes / 1 computer at once; largest machine 4 vCPU / 8 GB; always-on "No, sleeps when idle", so timeout_sec max 24 h applies (miosa.ai/pricing, 2026-11-08). The $1 is encoded here as included_usd (free.monthly_credit stays 0 so paid plans do not get it too).

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: "$20 a month with $20 of usage included, then pay as you go." 50 sandboxes / 5 computers at once; largest machine 4 vCPU / 8 GB; always-on yes (miosa.ai/pricing, 2026-11-08). The API reference still lists a 10-sandbox cap for Developer.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: $500 a month counted as usage; "Usage past the included credit bills at the same rates." 250 sandboxes / 50 computers at once; largest machine 8 vCPU / 16 GB; always-on yes (miosa.ai/pricing, 2026-11-08).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: $2,000 a month counted as usage, self-serve ("Choose Enterprise"). 1,000 sandboxes / 200 computers at once; largest machine 16 vCPU / 32 GB; always-on yes (miosa.ai/pricing, 2026-11-08). The API reference still lists 500 sandboxes for Enterprise. BAAs for Enterprise customers (/docs/faq/security-and-compliance).

extras.price: free (pricing FAQ: "No. Builds are free."; another FAQ line still says builds bill per minute)
per model, per 1M tokens: Kimi K2.6 $1.90 in / $8.00 out, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.60 / $2.40, GLM-5.3 $2.80 / $8.80
first 10 per organization included, then $1.70/month each, plus $0.018/GB-month stored

perf_source: ComputeSDK (each provider at its SDK default size and runtime): burst 73 ms median at 100 at once, 100% succeeded (2026-11-06); DAX clone + install + typecheck 34.17 s (2026-11-06, one run; sandbox saw 8 CPUs / 16 GiB x86). https://github.com/computesdk/benchmarks/tree/main/results
caveats: Prices from miosa.ai/pricing (2026-11-08), 1 credit = $0.01. The page publishes a price per size, not per vCPU or per GB of RAM. Disk bills at $0.09/GB-month while a machine runs and is folded into each size hour; micro, tiny and quad publish no disk size, so their hour has no disk part.
Paused or stopped: no compute; disk bills at the snapshot rate, $0.018/GB-month (encoded as snapshot_gib_month). Named snapshots: first 10 per organization included, then $1.70/month each.
Plan fee = usage credit (Developer $20, Business $500, Enterprise $2,000), so a paid plan costs max(fee, usage). Free gives $1 of usage a month and pauses machines at a $0 balance.
Largest machine by plan: 4 vCPU / 8 GB on Free and Developer, 8 / 16 on Business, 16 / 32 on Enterprise (miosa.ai/pricing).

Concurrency differs by resource type: Free 5 sandboxes / 1 computer, Developer 50 / 5, Business 250 / 50, Enterprise 1,000 / 200 (miosa.ai/pricing). Plan concurrency holds the sandbox cap, so the Computer mode is checked against a cap that is too high for it. The API reference still lists 10 / 250 / 500 sandboxes for Developer / Business / Enterprise.

Session length: timeout_sec 1-86400 s (default 3600). always_on: true disables timeout and idle-timeout enforcement, subject to tenant policy; pricing shows always-on on Developer and up, not on Free.
Idle auto-pause: idle_timeout_sec defaults to 1800 s for accounts created on or after 2026-10-11 and to 0 (off) for older accounts.
BYOC (AWS or Google Cloud) runs workers in your own cloud account; activation is gated per region on a provider canary, and no BYOC rate is published, so no BYOC mode is priced.
Isolation: the sandbox API says "isolated microVM workspaces"; Firecracker is named on the snapshots page (pause runtime) and the BYOC page. The SOMA runtime is early access and has no pause.
GPU: not offered as a product; no GPU rate on the pricing page (/docs/known-limitations).
Pricing FAQ conflicts on builds: one line says builds bill per minute, another says "Builds are free."
Regions: 3 US regions (us-west, us-east, us-mia), no multiplier. EU and APAC "on the roadmap" (miosa.ai/docs/api-reference/regions, 2026-10-14).

fleet.verification: Free plan: $1 of usage a month, no monthly charge; machines pause at a $0 balance. Paid plans charge the card on file before anything pauses.
fleet.tiers: Free 5 sandboxes / 1 computer at once; Developer ($20) 50 / 5; Business ($500) 250 / 50; Enterprise ($2,000) 1,000 / 200.
fleet.notes: Concurrency is per resource type (sandboxes vs Computers). The API reference (miosa.ai/docs/api-reference/sandboxes) still says "Plan cap: 10 (Developer), 250 (Business), 500 (Enterprise)", lower than the pricing page. All plans are self-serve.

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshots are taken on lifecycle events (stop, pause, fork) and on request.
snapshot_auto.note: Periodic automatic snapshots are not promised. Pause keeps memory and processes for up to 30 minutes on a runtime that advertises pause (Firecracker), then behaves like a stop. Memory checkpoints expire 72 h after a pause. The latest stop snapshot is kept for the life of the sandbox. Computers: "Restarting resumes from the snapshot" (/docs/computers/lifecycle).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots capture the full in-memory state of a running computer - CPU state, RAM, and filesystem - and store it durably. Restore a snapshot to spin up an identical computer in seconds.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Sandboxes: "Public V1 includes customer-managed snapshot create, list, show, delete, and restore" plus pause, resume and fork (/docs/known-limitations, 2026-11-08). Restore creates a new sandbox; in-place revert "is not available yet" (/docs/develop/snapshots). Named snapshots: first 10 per organization included, then $1.70/month each (miosa.ai/pricing).

harness_api.quote: Agent Runs are the prompt-dispatch interface for MIOSA sandboxes and computers. Use them when your product needs to send a natural-language task into a device, run it through OSA, Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Hermes, or a custom runtime, and receive a stable run response your UI can render.
harness_api.note: POST /api/v1/agent-runs (provider: osa, codex, claude/claude-code, pi, hermes, custom), durable events + SSE stream (GET /agent-runs/{id}/events?stream=true), cancel, artifacts, Agent Run Groups for multi-agent orchestration, runtime profiles; CLI 'miosa agent run --sandbox/--computer', 'miosa sandbox prompt'. Runtime-routing guide also lists Gemini CLI / OpenCode as customer-provided runtimes. No documented follow-up/resume-conversation endpoint; each run is a prompt dispatch.

egress_allowlist.quote: Pattern kinds: exact (literal host), wildcard (*.example.com), cidr (IP literal targets only).
egress_allowlist.note: Egress policies per Computer/Sandbox with mode audit_only/enforce and default_action allow/deny ('Tenant default starts in audit_only mode'), enforced by the host-side proxy. Computers additionally have /computers/{id}/network-policy with modes unrestricted/allowlist/denylist/isolated, host+port+protocol rules: 'Network policies apply at the microVM level.' Allowlist suggestions from the audit log.

egress_http_rules.note: Allowlist rules carry method and path_glob in addition to host; warn_only and priority fields. No header-level rules documented. Audit log records method/path per request.

ingress_rules.quote: Requires either an authenticated MIOSA session OR a valid share token.
ingress_rules.note: Preview URLs per port ({port}-{slug}.sandbox.miosa.ai) with public/private visibility, short-lived share tokens (preview_token, stripped by the proxy), preview tokens for iframes, custom preview domains. No IP allowlist documented.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM ('isolated microVM workspaces', /docs/api-reference/sandboxes) with root (exec default cwd /root, sudo apt-get in examples); nftables/iptables inside not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: the MIOSA proxy on your VM’s host sees the request, finds miosa-tok-7f2a8c1d4b2e6f0a in the Authorization header, and swaps it with your real sk-proj-... before forwarding to OpenAI. OpenAI sees the real key. Your sandbox never did.
secret_proxy.note: Any API key (example uses OpenAI and Stripe), plus OAuth Connect tokens with auto-refresh; placeholder swapped in headers, query params, URL paths and buffered bodies; rotation without restart; 5 scope levels; per-request audit. Docs claim it works with 'curl, requests, fetch, axios, gRPC' at the network layer; databases/SSH/git-over-SSH not mentioned. Per-secret host binding (which destinations may receive the real value) not documented.

volume_attach.quote: Create a persistent block device, attach it to a compatible computer on the same host, and preserve writes independently of the computer lifecycle.
volume_attach.note: Computers (and App Engine runtime instances); local-backend ext4, max 500 GB, 10 per project, host-bound. /docs/known-limitations (2026-11-08) still labels Volumes Beta: "Local volumes live on one host, so cross-host attach returns an error". Not documented for Sandboxes.

image_oci.quote: When the built-in catalog does not fit - proprietary toolchains, specific CUDA/GPU stacks, pre-loaded datasets - you can build and register your own template. 1. Write a Dockerfile for your image. 2. Build it using the custom sandbox template API...
image_oci.note: MIOSA builds a custom template FROM a Dockerfile you supply (not a direct pull of an existing pre-built OCI image/registry ref); once registered, sandboxes/computers boot from that image via template_id. Docker/BuildKit OCI-rootfs build path in the standard runtime is still 'hardening' per known-limitations.

anti_bot.quote: Create a Computer, wait until it is ready, connect to its desktop, complete browser work, and preserve evidence.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. MIOSA ships a generic Xfce desktop/browser for computer-use agents; no stealth/fingerprinting-evasion feature against bot detection is documented anywhere in the docs or llms-full.txt.

captcha_solving.quote: Use them for any task that benefits from a real GUI: browser automation, scraping JS-heavy sites, working behind logins, OCR/CAPTCHA loops, or operating desktop apps.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. CAPTCHA handling is presented as something YOU build with your own agent driving the desktop (OCR/CAPTCHA loops), not a built-in CAPTCHA-solving service/API.

egress_ip_type.quote: Egress policies per Computer/Sandbox with mode audit_only/enforce ... enforced by the host-side proxy.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: MIOSA sandboxes/computers are standard cloud-hosted firecracker microVMs (US regions us-west/us-east/us-mia) behind a host-side egress proxy; no residential/mobile IP product is offered or documented.

fork_running.quote: POST /sandboxes/{id}/fork creates a new sandbox from a copy-on-write snapshot of a running sandbox.
fork_running.note: Fork operates on a running sandbox without stopping it (copy-on-write snapshot of the live sandbox); memory_snapshot_fork is already true in the card.

wake_on_request.quote: Exec, file operations, and deploys on a stopped or paused persistent sandbox resume it first and then run, and a preview request wakes it and is held for up to 10 seconds before a 503 with Retry-After . A non-persistent sandbox is never auto-resumed and the call returns 409 .
wake_on_request.note: Sandboxes only, persistent ones (the default). Same page: "a stopped sandbox wakes on the next request". /docs/develop/previews does not mention it. Not documented for Computers, so the computer mode keeps wake_on_request null.

volume_shared.quote: Shared state across multiple replicas - volumes are typically attached to ONE runtime instance.
volume_shared.note: Volumes are explicitly host-bound and single-attach; cross-host attach to another machine returns an error rather than sharing.

own_agent_api.quote: Agent Runs are the prompt-dispatch interface for MIOSA sandboxes and computers. Use them when your product needs to send a natural-language task into a device, run it through OSA, Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Hermes, or a custom runtime, and receive a stable run response your UI can render.
own_agent_api.note: MIOSA's own 'OSA' task/browser/computer-use agent is one of the selectable providers driven through this first-party Agent Runs API (alongside coding harnesses like Codex/Claude Code); this is distinct from harness_api which covers the coding-harness case.

public_ipv4.quote: A Preview is a URL that routes to a port inside a running Sandbox.
public_ipv4.note: Ingress is via proxied preview URLs (port-slug.sandbox.miosa.ai) and egress via a host-side proxy, not a raw public IPv4 per machine; card's network.ipv4_available is also false. MIOSA's own comparison page (docs/integrations/comparison) lists 'Dedicated IPv4: per machine' for itself, which conflicts with the proxy-based architecture documented elsewhere and could not be corroborated with a concrete API field, so treated as unconfirmed marketing shorthand.

soc2.quote: Not yet. Our SOC 2 audit is in progress and not complete, so there is no report to share today.
soc2.note: A controls questionnaire is available under NDA until the report is issued.

hipaa.quote: business associate agreements (BAAs) are available for Enterprise customers
hipaa.note: BAA on Enterprise only (quote is cut at the page's line wrap; continues "...customers").

nested_virt.quote: KVM and QEMU cannot run inside a sandbox.
nested_virt.note: Explicit, unambiguous known-limitation for the Firecracker sandbox product.

custom_image.quote: When the built-in catalog does not fit — proprietary toolchains, specific CUDA/GPU stacks, pre-loaded datasets — you can build and register your own template. 1. Write a Dockerfile for your image. 2. Build it using the custom sandbox template API (or the CLI: `miosa sandbox-templates create`). 3. Verify the image boots correctly. 4. Register the slug so it is selectable in `template_id`.
custom_image.note: Documented Dockerfile-based custom template workflow. Caveat: the API reference (docs/api-reference/sandboxes) says 'Standalone custom-template build and promotion operations are not part of canonical public V1... Contact MIOSA for preview access', so this is a real but gated/preview capability, not a self-serve public V1 feature. Card should record true with that gating caveat rather than a flat false.

auto_stop_idle.quote: idle_timeout_sec integer Seconds without activity before the sandbox pauses. 0 disables it; accounts created on or after October 11, 2026 default to 1800 (30 minutes) when unset.
auto_stop_idle.note: On by default (30 min) for accounts created on or after 2026-10-11; older accounts default to 0 (off). Range 0-86400. On Firecracker the idle timeout pauses; a pause lasts up to 30 min, then behaves like a stop (/docs/develop/snapshots).

gpu.quote: The public sandbox create contract does not accept, persist, or schedule GPU requests.
gpu.note: GPU runtime exists behind a feature flag only; the pricing page lists no GPU rate.

windows.quote: Boot a Debian 12 microVM (Python + Node). ... computer = client.computers.create(template="ubuntu-desktop")
windows.note: Managed Sandboxes are Debian 12 microVMs and managed Computers boot Ubuntu desktop templates; Windows only appears via OpenComputers (bring-your-own hardware you already own), not as a MIOSA-provisioned OS.

macos.quote: It can be a workstation, a GPU machine, an on-premises server, or a supported existing server at a hosting provider. ... miosa opencomputers connect my-mac --platform macos
macos.note: macOS is only reachable by connecting a customer-owned Mac as an OpenComputer; MIOSA does not provision macOS machines itself. Managed Sandboxes/Computers are Linux-only (Debian/Ubuntu).

arm64.quote: The OSA prebuilt Linux target is x86-64. For Linux ARM64, follow the OSA source installation instructions rather than assuming the prebuilt installer supports it.
arm64.note: Managed Sandboxes/Computers are x86_64 (perf benchmark note in card also says '8 vCPU / 15.6 GiB x86_64 env'). ARM64 is only mentioned for a customer's own OpenComputer host running the agent from source, not a MIOSA-provisioned ARM machine.

self_host.quote: OpenComputers connects your machine to the MIOSA control plane. It is not an air-gapped deployment or a self-hosted copy of the complete MIOSA platform.
self_host.note: Explicit denial that any customer-run mode is a self-hosted copy of MIOSA; the control plane is always MIOSA-operated SaaS.

open_source.note: The OSA on-host agent binary is Apache-2.0 open source, and BusinessOS is an open-source reference app, but the core MIOSA platform (control plane/API/sandbox orchestration that this card prices) is closed SaaS — confirmed by the self_host quote above. false is correct for the core product; OSA-the-agent being OSS is a narrower fact.

sso.note: Also: 'Auth-as-a-Service Beta ... Refresh tokens, magic links, OAuth providers, MFA, passkeys, and enterprise SSO are still planned.' Note this conflicts with the card's own Enterprise plan note claiming 'SSO/SCIM' for Enterprise — that plan note appears to be aspirational/incorrect per the docs; sso should stay false.

eu_data_residency.quote: Yes - EU and APAC regions are on the roadmap. When they ship they'll appear in GET /api/v1/regions alongside the current three.
eu_data_residency.note: Only 3 US regions live (us-west, us-east, us-mia); EU is roadmap only.

live_resize.quote: POST /api/v1/computers/{id}/resize — Changes the vCPU and memory allocation. The computer must be stopped first.
live_resize.note: Resize exists but explicitly requires stopping the machine first, i.e. it is not a live/hot resize of a running instance.

docker_inside.quote: Every sandbox ships Docker with the docker compose and docker buildx plugins.
docker_inside.note: Page lists docker run, docker compose up -d and docker buildx build as working; default miosa-sandbox template ships Docker Engine 29.9 with Compose and Buildx. Known-limitations agrees: "Every sandbox ships Docker with the docker compose and docker buildx plugins, so you can build and test a container image there." (/docs/known-limitations). App Engine is only the path for durable containerized deployments.

static_egress_ip.quote: By default, every new MIOSA sandbox runs in audit-only mode: every outbound call is recorded, none are blocked. ... Mode flips to enforce. The proxy now blocks anything not on the list.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: MIOSA's egress control is a host-side allow/deny proxy (audit_only/enforce with allowlist rules) documented in full API reference (docs/api-reference/egress) and network-policy pages; nowhere in the docs, pricing page, or the 46k-line llms-full.txt is a fixed/static/dedicated outbound IP address mentioned as a product feature. network.ipv4_available is already false in the card and public_ipv4 is false; no separate static-egress-IP product or add-on is documented.

usage_api.quote: Returns measured runtime, provisioned vCPU time, active CPU, network traffic, estimated cost
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; Sandbox usage endpoint documented in API reference

persist_scope.quote: A stopped computer is not billed for compute; its disk is billed at $0.018 per GiB-month while it is stopped.
persist_scope.note: The whole disk survives a stop, installed packages included.

zero_data_retention.quote: Egress audit events are retained 90 days. Usage and credit records are kept separately. There is no published zero-retention mode.

max_session_h.quote: always_on: true disables timeout and idle-timeout enforcement until an explicit lifecycle action, subject to tenant policy.
max_session_h.note: Without always_on, timeout_sec is 1-86400 s (default 3600) (/docs/api-reference/sandboxes). Pricing marks always-on "Yes" on Developer, Business and Enterprise and "No, sleeps when idle" on Free, so the Free plan keeps max_session_h 24.

byoc.quote: general production activation remains gated on a real provider canary and per-host acceptance evidence.
byoc.note: AWS and Google Cloud only (no Azure). Your cloud bills the compute; MIOSA "Reports MIOSA usage separately" and publishes no BYOC rate. Pricing: each region is "installed and accepted with you before it takes production work".
